live_smoke_opt_in.detail: apps/codecamp-advantage/lib/__tests__/prod-smoke/_helpers/live-smoke-guard.ts has no production URL default and no credential default. RUN_LIVE_SMOKE is true only when process.env.RUN_LIVE_SMOKE === 'true'. resolveLiveSmokeUrl(envVarName) returns undefined unless both RUN_LIVE_SMOKE is true and the requested env var is a non-empty string. All 14 phase-*.test.ts files use resolveLiveSmokeUrl('PHASEn_PROD_URL') ?? '' and gate live probes with RUN_LIVE_SMOKE. When the gate is closed, 200 live probes skip (not silently pass). When the gate is open but no URL is supplied, the beforeAll https:// assertion fails the suite. The static report-summary.json still records the historical prod URL but carries a _runLiveSmokeNote token so the guard recognizes it as live-aware.

no_hardcoded_prod_smoke_secrets.detail: No real API keys, passwords, tokens, or webhook secrets are hardcoded in the helper or phase files. Phase 4/5/9/10 use environment variables for live credentials (PHASEn_TEST_*_USERNAME/PASSWORD, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, etc.). A handful of obviously dummy strings ('phase4-test-password-1234', 'wrong-password-for-phase10-concurrent-test', 'roundtrip-secret-123') are used only for test-created accounts or HMAC fixtures and are not production secrets.

opt_in_gate_not_bypassable.detail: The gate requires the exact string 'true' in RUN_LIVE_SMOKE. There is no --run-live flag, no FORCE_LIVE_SMOKE shortcut, and no default URL that would cause CI to hit production. PHASEn_SKIP=1 is an explicit opt-out, not a bypass.

marketing_credential_leak_guard.detail: The deterministic ENCRYPTION_KEY hex literal in phase-3-settings-adversarial.test.ts is a test-only fallback, not a real secret. The adversarial test's test-connection error-body case genuinely exercises leak prevention: it simulates an AI SDK error containing the caller's API key and asserts the response body does not contain it. The route at apps/marketing/app/api/settings/test-connection/route.ts redacts caller-supplied secrets with [REDACTED]. A contradictory 'NOT a real secret' comment was also present in phase-3-settings.test.ts (split across lines, evading the automated guard); Review B fixed it to match the adversarial file's fallback-purpose wording.

passWithNoTests_removal_honest.detail: Removing --passWithNoTests did not expose a hidden security gap. codecamp-advantage runs 44 test files / 1068 tests; the only failures are pre-existing RED from codecamp_qa_prod_20260517 (phase-8-5, phase-12, phase-13) and thai-text-width, all documented as out-of-scope in plan.md. sales-advantage runs 4 files / 24 tests and passes. @reading-advantage/scripts had zero tests; removing its vacuous 'jest --passWithNoTests' script was honest.

findings.title: phase-3-settings.test.ts contained a contradictory 'NOT a real secret' comment
findings.description: The same file that sets the deterministic ENCRYPTION_KEY fallback had a line-comment claiming 'This is NOT a real secret'. The wave2-test-truthfulness guard did not flag it because the banned phrase was split across two // comment lines. This is the same anti-pattern the phase intended to remove from phase-3-settings-adversarial.test.ts.
findings.fixDetail: Rewrote the comment to describe the fallback purpose without the banned phrase, matching the adversarial test's wording. Re-ran marketing truthfulness, phase-3-settings, and phase-3-settings-adversarial tests; all pass.

findings.title: GET /api/settings still decrypts and returns the API key without authentication
findings.description: apps/marketing/app/api/settings/route.ts GET() decrypts secret settings and returns them to any caller. This is the documented Wave 3 marketing security finding and is not fixed by Phase 3.
findings.fixDetail: Owned by Wave 3 (wave3_product_alignment_20260628 / marketing_golive_20260701) per measure/tracks.md. The Phase 3 changes only address encryption-at-rest and error-body redaction; they correctly do not claim to close the GET leak.

findings.title: opt-in-gated.fixture.ts still hardcodes the production URL as a fallback
findings.description: The 'good' counterexample fixture at wave2-fixtures/opt-in-gated.fixture.ts declares const PROD_URL = process.env.PHASEX_PROD_URL ?? 'https://codecamp.reading-advantage.com'. It is only a fixture and is not executed, but it models the exact live-default pattern the guard is meant to prevent.
findings.fixDetail: Not a runtime vulnerability because the fixture is not scanned by the live-default guard (subdirectory) and is never run. It could mislead future authors and should be cleaned up in a Wave 6 test-quality pass.

findings.title: Contradictory-credential-comment guard can be evaded by splitting the banned phrase across comment lines
findings.description:
wave2-test-truthfulness.test.ts line-checks each // line individually. A comment like '// This is NOT a real
// secret' avoids the literal match while still making the claim.
findings.fixDetail: Review B caught the evasion manually and fixed the only instance. Hardening the guard to span line boundaries is a test-quality improvement for Wave 6, not a Phase 3 blocker.

A2_consent_blind_publish_gate.detail: Phase 3 does not introduce or modify any draft -> published status gate. No consent/anonymization check is required.

A5_false_claim_text_vs_test_reality.detail: plan.md Phase 3 claims the targeted test commands exit 0. Verified: wave2-live-smoke-opt-in, wave2-test-truthfulness, phase-3-settings-adversarial, sales full suite, and config signal-inventory all exit 0.

A6_registry_overstatement.detail: measure/tracks.md does not claim Phase 3 or the marketing GET /api/settings leak is 'resolved'. The GET leak is explicitly listed as a Wave 3 / marketing-golive hard gate. No marketing copy outruns implementation.

A7_over_broad_filter.detail: New guard tests use precise regexes and path-based exclusions, not bare English exclusion words.

handoff: Phase 3 passes the security/data-handling review. The live-smoke opt-in gate has no production URL or credential default and cannot be trivially bypassed in CI. The marketing credential-leak comment was fixed in both the adversarial file and the sibling phase-3-settings.test.ts; the adversarial test still genuinely guards the test-connection error-body leak. Removing passWithNoTests exposed no hidden security gap. The one remaining real security issue is the unauthenticated GET /api/settings decrypted-API-key leak, which is correctly owned by Wave 3 and was not introduced or claimed fixed by Phase 3.
